sonnet.reason: Both involve a lack of time pressure, but abundant free time is about having an open schedule with few obligations, while unhurried is a pace and attitude that someone could have even when busy, or lack despite free time.

opus.reason: Abundant free time describes an open, unobligated schedule, while unhurried is an unrushed attitude toward tasks; they share the sense that nothing presses but are different kinds of things.

sonnet.reason: Both involve being unobtrusive, but one is about minimizing imposition on others' time and needs, while the other is about avoiding attention and the spotlight; either can occur without the other.

opus.reason: Both are about keeping oneself unobtrusive, but avoiding being a bother is about not imposing on others' time and needs, while self-effacing is about deflecting attention and recognition from oneself.

sonnet.reason: Both involve being unobtrusive, but the target is about not imposing on others' time and needs, while unassuming is about modest, unshowy self-presentation; each can occur without the other.

opus.reason: Both involve being unobtrusive and preferring to go unnoticed, but one is about not burdening others' time and needs while the other is about modest, unshowy self-presentation.

sonnet.reason: Both involve bending toward others' needs, but avoiding being a bother is about minimizing imposition and unobtrusiveness, while accommodating is about readily yielding positions to keep the peace; neither implies the other.

opus.reason: Both defer to others' needs, but minimizing one's own imposition differs from yielding one's positions to keep the peace.

sonnet.reason: Both mean standing by others at personal cost; 'loyal' is the same core but broader in scope (partner, team, secrets, not switching sides), while 'devoted to friends' is focused on friends.

opus.reason: Loyal is the same steadfast faithfulness at personal cost, only broader in scope, covering partner and team as well as friends, and adding secrecy and refusing to switch sides.

sonnet.reason: Both involve an unhurried, easy manner in conversation, but being easy to confide in adds nonjudgmental listening and discretion, while laid-back adds low-stakes casualness and neither implies the other.
Both involve warmth toward others, but being easy to confide in adds non-judgmental listening and discretion, while friendly adds general goodwill and sociability; neither implies the other.

opus.reason: Both involve warmth, but being easy to confide in centers on safe, nonjudgmental listening and discretion, while friendliness is general goodwill and eagerness to talk; each can exist without the other.

sonnet.reason: Both involve a warm, non-judgmental manner, but being easy to confide in centers on safe listening and keeping secrets, while gentleness centers on mild, kind handling and restraint in criticism; each has elements the other lacks.

opus.reason: Both share a warm, non-judgmental manner, but confidability adds safe listening and discretion with secrets, while gentleness adds soft handling of hard truths and restraint from cutting remarks, so neither implies the other.

sonnet.reason: Unhurriedness is one component of the target's warm, unhurried manner, but the target also requires non-judgmental listening and discretion, while unhurried is a general pace trait not tied to openness or trust.

Both involve warmth toward others, but being easy to confide in is about being a safe, nonjudgmental, discreet listener, while compassion is about empathic care for others' suffering; either can exist without the other.

Both describe choosing to be alone, declining invitations, and keeping others at a distance; the target adds keeping feelings and affairs private, while the other adds doing activities alone without regret.

opus.reason: Both describe preferring to be alone and declining company; withdrawn adds keeping feelings private, while solitary stresses doing everything alone by choice, so they are nearly the same concept with differing emphasis.

sonnet.reason: Both involve poor coping, but one is about being overwhelmed by ordinary daily tasks and the other about being easily destabilized by criticism or setbacks; each can occur without the other.

Both involve getting through days poorly, but the target is about being overwhelmed by chores and responsibilities, while languishing is about aimlessness, hollowness and disconnection, so each has features the other lacks.
Both describe interpreting words in their plain, direct sense without seeking figurative or implied meaning, so either label could replace the other.
